_comment: What's new in Golden Eye, shown in Settings → Updates. Newest first. Written for the people using the dashboard, not as commit messages. Add an entry in the same commit as the change it describes. area: SEO | Reports | Onboarding | Tasks | Security | Data. action: only when something has to be run or deployed before it works.

updates.title: Master GHL account setup, first step
updates.what: The master GHL account (the one every client account will be copied from) now has every custom value the onboarding questionnaire will fill. 12 were added, and where Master already had its own name for one (business name, Google review link, hours and so on) that one is used instead of a duplicate. It also has lead fields (project timeline, estimated budget, how they heard about us, homeowner, financing interest), fields for two cost quizzes (kitchen remodel and home builder, ready for a quiz survey to map to), and a simple Lead Pipeline (New lead to Won or Lost) as a starting point. A behind-the-scenes function does this and only ever touches the master account, never a client's.

updates.title: Onboarding questions that pick the right video
updates.what: Questions steps can now show a follow-up only when an earlier answer calls for it, save answers as you type, and check phone numbers, emails and links. Two new facts on every client (do they have a Facebook page, do they want leads sent to a CRM) can now decide which onboarding videos and tasks a client gets: tag a step with the answers it is for in Templates → Client Onboarding, and try a combination in Preview a Client. Nothing changes for clients yet: the Quick start step and the tasks for us are hidden until you switch them on with supabase/sql/onboarding_quick_start_go_live.sql.
updates.note: Choices in a question cannot contain commas.
updates.action: Run supabase/sql/onboarding_facts.sql

updates.title: A text when the daily ad pull comes up short
updates.what: Each morning at 13:30 UTC (7:30 Mountain in summer) the database checks that every client who normally has ad data also has yesterday's row, and texts Tenny the names of any that are missing, so a failed Make run is caught within a couple of hours instead of by hand. The Make pull itself now carries on past one client's failure, and the Make-limit notice on the Overview now warns at 100 clients, the real limit.
updates.action: Run supabase/sql/daily_pull_check.sql

updates.title: The office: who is online and what they are doing
updates.what: Settings → Users & Roles has a little office, hidden until you click Show characters. Make your character (My character), and when you have Golden Eye open you appear at your desk, typing, on the phone, reviewing creatives or looking at a client, depending on the page you are on. Step away and you grab a coffee, close the tab and you go to sleep in the Off duty row. Type what you are up to in the box and it shows in a speech bubble for four hours.
updates.note: Only admins can see it, and a client's browser never learns who is on the team.
updates.action: Run supabase/sql/team_presence.sql

updates.title: Older clients no longer show our onboarding steps as outstanding
updates.what: A client who has moved past Onboarding now shows our own onboarding steps (Get ready for GHL, Set up GHL) as done in their Onboarding Progress, instead of "No task yet". For their own steps, use Mark client steps done at the top of that box.

updates.title: A loading screen
updates.what: Golden Eye now shows a loading screen with the logo and a progress bar while it signs you in and loads your clients, instead of flashing the sign-in card first. If something is slow it says so and offers a Reload button.
updates.note: The dashboard's own half of this is live as soon as it is pushed. To also cover the first second, before the dashboard arrives, paste the updated goldeneye.html into the GHL page again.
updates.action: Optional: re-paste goldeneye.html into the GHL page to cover the very first second.

updates.title: Our checklist for every new client
updates.what: Everything we do after a client finishes onboarding is now a checklist: getting ready for GHL (answers, Facebook access, Meta sync, target CPL), setting up GHL (account, A2P first, funnel, workflows, people, tests) and launching ads. On the board it shows as three tasks per client. Open a client's Health tab and press Our checklist, in the Journey box or on the highlighted onboarding row, to see every step, tick them off, or open one as a task to assign someone. A group ticks itself when its last step is done, and a few steps tick themselves.
updates.note: Steps are tagged Base or Ads, so a Base-only client skips the Meta and funnel steps. They are hidden from the client's portal. A client now reaches Campaign Building once GHL is set up, and launching ads is the Campaign Building checklist, instead of an onboarding task. Clients who finished earlier do not get one.
updates.action: Run supabase/sql/setup_checklist.sql. Then redeploy the overview chat so it ignores the steps: supabase functions deploy overview-chat --project-ref hugnttsqucetldllfgoi

updates.title: A warning when you reach Make's client limit
updates.what: Make's daily ads pull reads clients ten at a time, so the eleventh client with an ad account would silently get no ad data. The Overview now shows a notice when you reach ten active clients with an ad account, and a red one if you go past it, so you know to raise the limit in that Make scenario first.

updates.title: A second hidden game
updates.what: There is another secret. Admins who find it can race against the clock to answer leads. Faster replies score more, and the best scores are kept on a leaderboard.
updates.note: It is not documented here on purpose.
updates.action: Run supabase/sql/speed_lead_runs.sql so scores can be saved.

updates.title: Ask Golden Eye: a chat on the Overview page
updates.what: Ask anything about your clients in plain English, such as which ads are over their target CPL, what is overdue and who owns it, or how a client did against last week. It looks the numbers up live in ads, tasks, check-ins, website leads, SEO, onboarding and the morning audit, and shows which of those it used. It can only read, never change anything, and only admins see it.
updates.note: It does not see task notes or check-in replies. Each question uses the same OpenAI model as the morning audit, so a heavy question costs a little more than the old client chat.
updates.action: Deploy the function first: supabase functions deploy overview-chat --project-ref hugnttsqucetldllfgoi

updates.title: An activity panel on each client's Ads tab
updates.what: Below the charts, a client with synced ad data now shows what changed in their account (turned on or off, budget, targeting, creative, new ads), who did it, and what the affected ads did 7 days before and after. Next to it is every ad with its spend, share of spend, leads and cost per lead, with the CPL in red when it is at or over the client's target.
updates.note: Only admins see it. It follows the date range at the top, up to the last 120 days. Leads are Meta's own count, which can run higher than the daily pull for some clients.

updates.title: A journey bar on each client's Health tab
updates.what: Between Weekly Check-ins and Onboarding there is now a bar showing how close the client is to their next stage. In Onboarding it counts the same steps as the Onboarding list below it. In every later stage it counts that stage's checklist tasks, and a full bar says the client is ready to move on. You still move them with Move Stage.

updates.title: Text whoever a task is assigned to
updates.what: Open a task and press Text the assignee to send them a one-line text with the task, client and due date. It works for Aidan and Tenny now; "Tenny, Aidan" texts both. Someone with no number on file (KJ, the account manager) is named in the reply instead of failing.
updates.note: KJ's number (Philippines, +63) is included, so he can be texted too. The account manager still needs a number.
updates.action: Run supabase/sql/task_notify.sql in the SQL Editor.

updates.title: The morning audit says when ads are off, not that the data is broken
updates.what: A client whose ads were switched off used to be reported as "the daily pull looks broken", because the daily pull writes nothing for days with no spend. The audit now asks Meta: if it confirms there has been no spend for the last few days, the card says the ads have been off since that day and asks you to confirm it is intended. Real data problems are still reported as before.
updates.action: Deploy morning-audit

updates.title: Ad history loads in pieces when Meta refuses a big request
updates.what: Meta sometimes answers a large request for one account with "service temporarily unavailable". The ad sync now falls back to loading that account in one-week pieces, retries each once, and says which pieces did not load. It also stops cleanly before its time limit and names what is left, and can be told to skip straight to pieces and leave out days that are already loaded.
updates.action: Deploy meta-sync, then run the 90-day backfill again for Caliber Cabinets

updates.title: The morning audit lists ads at or over target
updates.what: Each morning the audit now also lists individual ads that are at or over their client's target cost per lead over the last 7 days, with spend, leads and a link to the ad in Ads Manager. It only flags: nothing is paused or changed. An ad is skipped while it is still new (under 4 days) or once it has stopped spending. Ad-level leads come from Meta, so they are scaled to match your daily pull for that client, and the card says when it did that. Clients without a target CPL are named, so you know their ads weren't checked.
updates.note: The line is "at or over target". If that flags too many, it is one setting in the audit code to move it to 1.5x or 2x.
updates.action: Set Target CPL on each client in Edit Client, then deploy morning-audit

updates.title: Client landing pages no longer count as Midas's own website leads
updates.what: Leads from client pages hosted on Midas's domain (Everoak, Astra) were being filed under Midas Media, so Midas's website leads looked like 43 when only 1 was. A client can now list which of its pages count as its own site, and Midas's list is its homepage and booking page. The mislabeled ones are removed. Other clients work as before.
updates.action: Run supabase/sql/lead_hosts.sql, then deploy ghl-lead-webhook

updates.title: Archiving a finished handoff task no longer triggers a second "onboarding complete" alert
updates.what: Golden Eye treated an archived "Onboarding complete" task as if it had never been raised, so archiving it for a client still in Onboarding filed a fresh one and texted you again. Archived tasks now count as already done. The client's own text was never affected, since it only goes out when they finish a step.

updates.title: Every admin can archive and edit tasks
updates.what: Only three named logins were allowed to change tasks, so for anyone else archiving, moving, editing or deleting a task could silently not save. Every admin can now manage tasks, and if a change is ever refused you now get a message instead of nothing.
updates.action: Run supabase/sql/tasks_admin_access.sql

updates.title: Board and List are different again, and the Board can archive
updates.what: Clicking List used to leave the Board showing, so the two looked the same and the List's checkboxes and Archive button were easy to miss. List now replaces the Board. The Board's Done column also has an Archive done button that archives every finished task the current filters show.

updates.title: Classified
updates.what: Something is hidden in Golden Eye. Agents only. Clicking the logo once now takes you to the overview.
updates.action: Run supabase/sql/egg_runs.sql

updates.title: VAs log weekly check-ins on the Roster
updates.what: Clients no longer get automated texts asking for their weekly numbers. Our VAs text them instead and log the answers: Roster (now its own tab in the sidebar) → open a client → Log check-in. Pick the week and who you texted, type in their estimates, jobs and revenue by where the customer came from, and paste their reply if you like. The Roster has a Check-in column (Logged, Client sent or Missing), and the tab's badge counts clients still missing last week's numbers. When we've logged a client's week, their portal shows those numbers instead of asking again, and their reports unlock.
updates.note: Each check-in records which of us logged it. This also closes a gap where any signed-in user could read every client's check-in numbers, and fixes most clients being unable to save a check-in from their portal.
updates.action: Run supabase/sql/staff_checkins.sql

updates.title: Archive tasks instead of deleting them, and a shorter Done column
updates.what: The task drawer's Delete button is now Archive, and the list view's bulk Delete is Archive too. An archived task leaves every board, count, report and the client's portal, but nothing is lost: open Tasks → Archived to restore it, or delete it for good from there. The Done column now shows the 8 most recently finished tasks, with View more at the bottom, instead of growing forever.
updates.note: Archiving also stops an onboarding or checklist task from being created again, which deleting didn't.
updates.action: Run supabase/sql/task_archive.sql, then re-run supabase/sql/auto_check_reconcile.sql, then deploy client-summary

updates.title: Reports say what we changed in the ads and what it did
updates.what: Golden Eye now keeps each ad's daily spend and leads, and Meta's change history for every client's ad account, refreshed every morning. Generate Report uses them: changes made during the week (an ad set turned off, a budget raised, a new ad launched) go in with what the affected ads did before and after, or "too early to tell" when it's only been a day or two, plus how each ad did. Who made a change is never named in a report.
updates.note: Only admins can see the change log and per-ad numbers. The Roster now opens on Active clients.
updates.action: Run supabase/functions/meta-sync/schema.sql and re-run supabase/sql/rename_client.sql, set META_ACCESS_TOKEN, deploy meta-sync, then run its schedule.sql

updates.title: Task filters: You, Midas, a person and a client
updates.what: The task page now has All, You, Ours, Client and Midas. You shows the tasks assigned to you (including ones shared with someone else), and Midas shows our own internal work. Two dropdowns narrow it further: pick a person to see their tasks, or a client to see theirs. The numbers across the top follow whatever you've picked, so You shows your own late and due-today counts. Your choice is remembered next time you open the page.
updates.note: Select-all in the list view now picks only the tasks on screen, so a bulk delete or status change can't touch tasks the filters are hiding. Also: the Roster opens a client's profile right under their row instead of a side panel, MRR is off the Roster, and the client portal's sales-team step asks for each person's email (optional).

updates.title: Roster: every client and everyone you deal with there
updates.what: View all on the overview's Active roster opens the Roster: every client with filters for active, paused and archived, and by service, plus search across client names and the people on file (name, email or phone). Click a client for their full profile: the owner, sales reps, office, website person and anyone else, each with a tap-to-call number and email; business phone, website and address; contract and billing; services; connections; onboarding answers; and private notes. Admins only.
updates.note: Each person has a Check-in texts switch. It's on for everyone already listed, so nothing changes for the weekly reminder, and off by default for new people, so a website person or bookkeeper can be on file without being texted. People are now edited on the Roster profile; Edit client shows who's on file and links there. This also closes a gap where any signed-in user could read or change any client's contacts.
updates.action: Run supabase/sql/client_directory.sql, then re-run supabase/sql/rename_client.sql

updates.title: Client records are private to each client
updates.what: A client signed into the portal could read every client's record (retainer, payment status, emails, ad account) and could change or delete any of them. Each client now sees only their own record, and only admins can add, edit or delete clients. Admins, the client portal and the investor's view work as before.
updates.note: Members no longer see the Save and Log Payment buttons on the Payments tab, since only admins can change payment details. Overdue payments are still flagged on screen for everyone, and saved as overdue when an admin loads the dashboard.
updates.action: Run supabase/sql/clients_rls_tests.sql (all 8 must pass), then supabase/sql/clients_rls.sql

updates.title: Target CPL and a spend rule for the morning audit
updates.what: Edit Client has a new Target CPL box. Set it and the morning audit judges that client against the cost per lead you expect instead of their own last 28 days, so an account that is consistently expensive no longer reads as fine. The audit also has a new spend rule: cost per lead at double the target (or double their usual, with no target) on $200 or more of spend in a week is Critical, even when there are too few leads to prove it statistically. Small accounts like 3Sixty and SimpliBlinds used to be marked too thin to judge, which hid exactly these weeks.
updates.note: Critical texts both admins, and the week slides forward daily, so a bad week can text you on several mornings in a row. Small accounts also swing week to week, so expect the odd text for a week that was just unlucky. Being under a target never counts as improving; that still means better than their own past.
updates.action: Deploy morning-audit (supabase functions deploy morning-audit), then set Target CPL on the clients that should have one

updates.title: Content ideas
updates.what: A new Content Ideas panel on the SEO tab lists real questions people search and phrases they use around a client's own top tracked searches — a starting list for the next article, refreshed once a month. Each idea shows where it came from, its search volume and how hard it'd be to rank for, when SE Ranking provides those numbers. Dismiss the ones that aren't worth writing; dismissed ideas stay out of the way (with a "Show dismissed" toggle) and are never brought back by the next refresh.
updates.note: This is the first SEO feature that spends SE Ranking's paid Data API units rather than the free rank-tracking API — sized at roughly 150-875 units per client per month against the 25,000/month budget, and it checks remaining units before running so it can never starve other SE Ranking features.
updates.action: Run supabase/sql/seo_content_ideas.sql, then supabase/sql/rename_client.sql, then deploy seranking-sync

updates.title: Printable SEO case studies
updates.what: A new Case Study button at the top of the SEO tab builds a one-page before-and-after: visits, leads, rankings, site sessions and revenue from before SEO started, now, and (once there's a full year of history) a year ago — with the work completed along the way. Print it or save it as a PDF straight from the preview.
updates.note: Anything that predates what measures it — leads before tracking began, rankings before a keyword was added, GA4 before it was connected — shows as not measured, never a false zero. A new Capture Baseline button saves exactly what's on screen as a permanent snapshot, so the number you tell a client at signing can't drift if Search Console later revises that period.
updates.action: Run supabase/sql/seo_case_study.sql

updates.title: A dedicated Map Pack section
updates.what: The admin SEO tab now has its own Map Pack panel: how many tracked searches are holding a spot in Google's local 3-pack, how many at #1, the average pack position, and a chart of that count day by day so you can see the pack forming or slipping over the week rather than a single snapshot. Each keyword lists its pack position, its organic position alongside it, and a per-city breakdown for keywords tracked from more than one town.
updates.note: For clients with Business Profile connected, it also shows Maps profile views for the same range, tying pack rank to real visibility.
updates.action: Run supabase/sql/seo_map_pack.sql

updates.title: Google Business Profile on the SEO tab
updates.what: A Business Profile section now sits under Site Analytics: calls, website clicks, direction requests, messages and profile views against the period before, actions per day, how much of the profile's visibility came from Search vs Maps, how people searched (the business name, or the service), the search terms that showed the profile, and the reviews still waiting for a reply with a link to answer them on Google.
updates.note: The data comes through SE Ranking's Local Marketing tool, free to read, so there's no waiting on Google's API approval. Each client's profile has to be added as a location in SE Ranking first. Midas is connected; set its SE Ranking Local ID (42103) under Edit.
updates.action: Run supabase/sql/gbp.sql, then supabase/sql/rename_client.sql, then deploy seranking-sync

updates.title: Site Analytics from Google Analytics
updates.what: The bottom of the SEO tab now has a Wix-style analytics section for clients with a GA4 property: site sessions, page views, average session length, pages per session, engaged visits, key events and post views, each against the period before. Below that: sessions over time, top traffic sources, visits from AI assistants like ChatGPT and the pages they landed on, top pages with time on page and exit rate, the pages visits start on, top posts, a navigation flow for any page (where people came from and where they went next), and form submissions.
updates.note: Exit rate and the navigation flow are close estimates worked out from where each page view came from. Form submissions only show once the site's form sends a GA4 event marked as a key event. Midas is connected; add 3Sixty's GA4 property ID under Edit.
updates.action: Run supabase/sql/ga4_analytics.sql, then supabase/sql/rename_client.sql, then deploy seo-sync

updates.title: The chat agent now knows a client's real SEO
updates.what: Ask the Client Intelligence Agent about a client's SEO and it now answers from the same numbers as the SEO tab: visits, position and leads from Google over the last 28 days, a 16-week weekly trend, the SEO work logged with dates, top pages, what moved, wrong pages ranking, competitors, and the latest site audit. Try "why did traffic change?" or "what should we work on next?". Before, it was reading an old table that stopped updating when Make's SEO pull was switched off.

updates.title: Client work summaries locked to their schedule
updates.what: The service that writes each client's daily work summary now only runs for its 16:05 schedule or a signed-in admin. Before, anyone who read the page's source could force it to rewrite every client's portal summary, using our OpenAI account. The daily summaries work as before.

updates.title: Morning audit locked to admins and its schedule
updates.what: The morning audit service now only answers a signed-in admin or its own 10am schedule. Before, anyone who read the page's source could pull every client's name, spend, leads and cost per lead from it, or force a new audit run that could text you both. The Run Morning Audit button, the chat's all-clients mode and the daily schedule all work as before.

updates.title: AI chat and reports locked to admins
updates.what: The AI behind the Client Intelligence Agent and Generate Report now only answers a signed-in admin. Before, anyone who read the page's source could use it to run requests on our OpenAI account, from any website. Chat replies are also shown as safe text now, so a task title containing code can't run in your browser, and the report preview in Generate Report can no longer run scripts. The chat and reports work exactly as before, on the same model.
updates.action: Deploy ai-chat (after this update is live)

updates.title: Monthly site audit
updates.what: The bottom of the SEO tab now shows the client's latest site audit from SE Ranking: a health score out of 100, errors, warnings and notices, and every issue found with how many pages it affects. Errors and warnings show first; notices are behind a button. From the second month on, it shows the change since last time — the score going up or down, issues that are new, counts that rose or fell, and what got fixed.
updates.note: SE Ranking now re-audits 3Sixty and Midas on the 1st of every month. That uses the plan's page allowance, not API units. 3Sixty's first audit scored 70 (57 errors, including 54 broken images); Midas scored 87.
updates.action: Run supabase/sql/seo_site_audits.sql, then supabase/sql/rename_client.sql, then deploy seranking-sync

updates.title: Competitor numbers fixed, directories hidden
updates.what: Fixed: a competitor who isn't in Google's top 100 was being counted as ranking #100, so every comparison said we were ahead. Midas showed "ahead on 14, behind on 0" against all five competitors when four of them don't rank for those searches at all. They now count as not ranking. "Who owns this market" also hides directories and manufacturers (Yelp, Houzz, Trex, booking widgets) by default, with a button to show them, so the list shows the local businesses worth tracking.
updates.action: Re-run supabase/sql/seo_competitors.sql (it also clears the bad rows), then deploy seranking-sync

updates.title: Competitors
updates.what: The SEO tab now tracks the other companies ranking for a client's searches. Admin side: one line per competitor (how many page-1 spots they hold, where we're ahead, where they are), a search-by-search grid, and "who owns this market" — every site in Google's top 10, sorted by how many of the client's cities it appears in. The client's Organic Search tab gets a plain "How you compare" section: how many shared searches they're ahead on, counts only, no jargon.
updates.note: 3Sixty now tracks Backyard Builders Utah, Blackrock Decks, TC Decks Utah, Eremos Decks and Quality Decking of Utah — chosen from SE Ranking's own top-10 data, not a guess. Competitor ranks are organic only; SE Ranking doesn't report their Google Maps spot. Data starts at the next daily check, since competitor history never backfills.
updates.action: Run supabase/sql/seo_competitors.sql, then supabase/sql/rename_client.sql, then deploy seranking-sync

updates.title: Rankings by city
updates.what: For clients tracked in more than one city, Tracked Keywords has a "Rankings from" picker. All cities shows each keyword's best spot, with a "N cities" button that opens that keyword's rank in every city. Pick one city to see the whole table, and the wrong-page alerts, from there. Alerts now name the city where the wrong page ranks.
updates.note: Also fixed: a keyword's ranking page could come from a different city than its rank. It now comes from the city with the best rank.
updates.action: Re-run supabase/sql/seo_admin_rpcs.sql

updates.title: Wrong-page alerts
updates.what: The SEO tab now warns when Google ranks a different page than the one you set as the target in SE Ranking, for example the blog list showing up instead of the deck repair page. Flagged keywords get a warning icon, and a summary above Tracked Keywords lists every mismatch with the page that is ranking and the page that should be.
updates.note: 3Sixty is set up for this: 5 cities tracked (Eagle Mountain, Lehi, Saratoga Springs, American Fork, Draper) and 53 keywords, each with a target page.

updates.title: Keywords follow your SE Ranking list
updates.what: Keywords you remove in SE Ranking now drop off the SEO tab and reports on the next sync (their history is kept). Each keyword's target page is also brought in from SE Ranking, ready for the wrong-page alerts.
updates.action: Deploy seranking-sync.

updates.title: A tidier SEO tab
updates.what: The SEO Changelog, Top Pages and Tracked Keywords now show their first three rows, with a View all button to open the rest. A list you open stays open while you change the date range.

updates.title: This Updates page
updates.what: Every change to Golden Eye in plain English, newest first, with anything still needing a SQL run or deploy marked Action needed. The tab shows a count of what's new since you last looked.

updates.title: Weekly reports now include real SEO results
updates.what: A report for an SEO client gets an Organic Search section built from the same numbers their SEO tab shows: visits and leads from Google, jobs they reported closing from Google, which searches moved up, searches sitting on page 2, and the articles and fixes that went live that week. Small numbers stay plain counts instead of being spun as percentages.
updates.note: Also fixed: the "period before" comparison was one day longer than the period being reported, which slightly inflated every prior-period figure here and on the SEO tab.

updates.title: Every Make automation now requires a secret
updates.what: Make webhook links are public, and anyone holding one could make Golden Eye text a client, draft an email, or overwrite an ad approval. All five now check a shared secret first, and the two that send texts look up contacts by exact phone match so one reminder can never reach several people.
updates.note: This also uncovered that admin alerts for client requests had never actually fired: the scenario was filtering on the wrong field. Fixed, so onboarding-complete and help requests now text you.

updates.title: Hide a task from the client
updates.what: Tick "Hide from client" on any task and it stays on your board, marked Hidden, but never shows in their portal, their weekly work summary or their report. Hidden is enforced in the database, not just on screen.
updates.action: Run supabase/sql/task_client_visibility.sql, then deploy client-summary.

updates.title: Forms you build inside Golden Eye
updates.what: A step can now be a set of questions answered right in the portal, with no GHL form and no Make scenario behind it. Write the questions in Templates, mark any as required, and show a question only for clients with an existing site or a new build. Answers appear on the client's page with a Copy button, ready to paste into Cuppa.
updates.action: Run supabase/sql/onboarding_questions.sql, then re-run supabase/sql/rename_client.sql.

updates.title: SEO onboarding steps, and hiding a step until it's ready
updates.what: The SEO Growth steps are in: an intake form and a Google access video for the client, and seven setup tasks for us. The eye button on any step hides it from clients, so a step can be drafted before its video or form exists.
updates.action: Run supabase/sql/seo_onboarding_steps.sql once.

updates.title: Tasks that tick themselves off
updates.what: Setup tasks close on their own once Golden Eye can see the work is done: the ad account is saved, spend is flowing, Search Console is syncing, the first article auto-logged, the first website lead arrived. Each carries a note saying why it closed. A lightning bolt marks which tasks work this way.
updates.action: Run supabase/sql/auto_check_reconcile.sql.

updates.title: Onboarding follows what each client actually bought
updates.what: Clients get the steps for their add-ons and website situation, nothing else. An SEO-only client never sees Facebook steps. Adding SEO to a long-standing client brings back Get Started with just the SEO steps, raises our SEO tasks when they finish, and doesn't re-announce their original onboarding.
updates.action: Run supabase/sql/service_onboarding.sql, then the trigger file and its tests.

updates.title: Services, step tags and a client preview in Templates
updates.what: Templates → Services manages the add-ons. Every onboarding step and stage checklist item can be tagged by add-on and website situation, and Preview a Client shows exactly what someone with, say, Ads + SEO and an existing site would get. Add/Edit Client gained add-on checkboxes and a website dropdown.

updates.title: The client SEO tab
updates.what: SEO clients now have a tab written for people who don't know SEO: what it did for their business, how far they've come since starting, a traffic chart marked with the work we did, their target searches in plain language, and what's next. A return-per-dollar figure appears only once it's genuinely positive.

updates.title: Articles log themselves
updates.what: Publishing on Webflow, Wix, Sanity or a GitHub-based site records itself in the SEO changelog, with markers on the traffic chart showing when each went live. Setup is about a minute per client from the SEO tab. Midas's 42 articles and 3Sixty's 55 posts were backfilled.

updates.title: Almost Page 1, and map-pack rankings counted properly
updates.what: The admin SEO tab lists searches sitting on page 2, which are the best content targets. Keyword rankings now count a map-pack placement as ranking, so a local client in the map pack no longer reads as "not ranking".

updates.title: Check-ins ask where each job came from
updates.what: The weekly check-in splits closed jobs and revenue by source: Google or your website, Facebook or Instagram ads, referrals, or other. Totals still work exactly as before, and the Google row is what powers the return figures on the SEO tab.

updates.title: Reports explain the work in the client's words
updates.what: "What We're Working On" is always included, with planned to-dos rewritten as plain language rather than pasted task titles, and no internal due dates or assignees. Notes you type are saved with the report, the summary reads casually, and a week with no prior spend is treated as a fresh baseline instead of compared to nothing.
